title: Capturing Membrane Dynamics and Spike Timing of Human Neurons at Scale using Neural Operators
abstract: arXiv:2611.06933v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Characterizing the properties of neuronal cell types is central to understanding brain function. Yet, biophysically realistic neuron models remain difficult to scale to large populations while preserving the richness of cellular dynamics and within-cell-type variability. We present a cell-type-specific neural-operator framework for scalable neuronal population modeling. Rather than training separate surrogate models for individual neurons, the proposed framework learns a shared operator across multiple modeled neurons from the same cell type, conditioned on biologically interpretable electrophysiological features. Relative to the original single-neuron \texttt{NOBLE} setting, learning across heterogeneous neurons requires a richer electrophysiological conditioning representation and a training objective designed to preserve diverse spiking dynamics. translated_title: 利用神经算子大规模捕捉人类神经元的膜动力学与锋电位时序
translated_abstract: 表征神经元细胞类型的特性是理解大脑功能的核心。然而，具有生物物理真实性的神经元模型难以扩展到大规模神经元群体，同时又能保持细胞动力学的丰富性以及细胞类型内部的变异性。我们提出了一个细胞类型特异性的神经算子框架，用于可扩展的神经元群体建模。该框架并非为每个单独的神经元训练独立的替代模型，而是在来自同一细胞类型的多个建模神经元上学习一个共享算子，并以生物学上可解释的电生理特征作为条件。相对于原始的单神经元NOBLE设置，跨异质神经元的学习需要更丰富的电生理条件表示，以及一个旨在保留多样锋电位动力学的训练目标。这使得能够高效生成大规模的胞体电压响应集合，同时……
tldr: 该论文提出一个细胞类型特异性的神经算子框架，通过在同类多个神经元模型上学习共享算子并以可解释的电生理特征为条件，实现大规模神经元群体建模，同时保留丰富的膜动力学、锋电位时序及细胞类型内变异性。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a cell-type-specific neural operator framework that learns a shared operator across multiple neurons of the same cell type, conditioned on biologically interpretable electrophysiological features, enabling scalable neuronal population modeling while preserving membrane dynamics, spike timing, and within-cell-type variability.
